result:
I rewrote `skills/delivering-an-initiative/SKILL.md`, committed it as `36ecb74`, and left the result as `DONE`.

The skill now starts `work run` as soon as it is asked, with no formulated-proposal precondition, and shows what `work run` printed. It drafts no work-items from proposals and makes no commit of its own. A trial's fix is the one thing it still drafts, with `work add`. It starts no `claude -p` session and merges no branch, even when `work run` fails. It puts a refused tool, a `failed` work-item or a `work: <why>` stop to the person as a question. The exit text now says `awaiting-answer` instead of `awaiting-ruling`.

All six requirements this work-item accepts (delivery r4, r10, r19, r20, r21, r22) are in a guarantees capability, so there is no scenario to go red or green. Review judges them against the new text. `python3 -m pytest -q --work-item w141` passed (142 passed, 1 skipped), and `tools size --limit 300` printed nothing.

Open questions, all in `report.md`:
- **r21 cannot fire yet.** `work run` doesn't print a refused tool, so that question can't come up until supervision does.
- **Empty list.** The exit-code-0 line ("every work-item green") may read wrongly when the initiative has no work-items.
- **`work run` refusing to start.** I left unchosen whether this is an r22 question or an r7 stop. The text treats it as a `work:` stop, which is a question.
- **Stale drafting lines in `README.md`.** Lines 57, 149, 206, 229 and 250 still describe the old drafting skill. `README.md` is outside this work-item's file set, so I didn't touch it.
